context: A Vitest project where the module double must return something different in each of three tests. Predicted baseline failure: the agent declares the fixture or the mock function at module scope and closes over it from the `vi.mock` factory. Vitest hoists that factory above the imports, so the module-scope binding is not initialised when the factory runs and the suite dies with a ReferenceError rather than failing an assertion. The two ways out are `vi.hoisted()` or importing the mocked module and steering it per test with `mockResolvedValue` / `mockRejectedValue`; an agent that does not know the hoisting rule tends to produce the broken shape and then, if it runs the suite, thrash on it.

checklist.name: Suite passes
checklist.description: `npm test` exits clean with all three new cases plus the existing format test executing. A ReferenceError from a hoisted `vi.mock` factory, or any other failure to collect, scores zero here - this is the criterion the hoisting rule actually decides.

checklist.name: The API module is mocked, not the network
checklist.description: `./api-client.js` is replaced with `vi.mock` (or the module's export is spied). Stubbing global `fetch` instead scores at most half: it works, but it tests through api-client's own error-mapping rather than isolating user-service, so a change in api-client breaks these tests for the wrong reason. Making a real network call scores zero.

checklist.name: Mock factory does not close over an uninitialised binding
checklist.description: If a `vi.mock` factory is used, any value it references is created inside the factory or via `vi.hoisted()`. A factory referencing a `const`/`let` declared at module scope scores zero, whether or not the author noticed - that is the hoisting defect, and it is the thing this scenario exists to detect.

checklist.name: Each case steers the double independently
checklist.description: The three tests each set the doubled function's behaviour for themselves - `mockResolvedValueOnce` / `mockRejectedValueOnce` or per-test `mockImplementation`. One shared factory implementation that branches on the id it receives scores at most half: it couples the three cases into one function that must be edited whenever any case changes.

checklist.name: 404 case asserts null rather than a throw
checklist.description: The not-found test asserts the resolved value is `null`. Asserting only that the call does not reject scores at most half - `undefined` would also satisfy that, and the mapping to `null` is the behaviour under test.

checklist.name: Propagation case asserts the error escapes
checklist.description: The third test asserts the call rejects, via `await expect(...).rejects` or an equivalent that fails when nothing is thrown. A try/catch whose catch block holds the only assertions scores zero: the test passes when `getUser` returns normally, which is precisely the regression it is meant to catch.

checklist.name: Mock state does not leak between tests
checklist.description: Doubles are reset between tests - `mockReset`/`mockClear` in a hook, `restoreMocks`/`clearMocks` config, or exclusive use of the `...Once` variants. Tests that rely on the previous test having consumed a queued value score zero.

checklist.name: No new dependencies and no test-file edits
checklist.description: MUST NOT add packages to package.json or modify src/format.test.js and src/api-client.js. The task states the double must work with what is installed.

checklist.name: Explicit vitest imports
checklist.description: The new file imports `test`/`expect`/`vi` from 'vitest' rather than relying on globals, matching the existing src/format.test.js and the project's lack of a `globals: true` setting.
